why: Only Apple WWDC25 (snapshot undo) is yes/yes; Cody and Elicit are vendor pages and the rest cover scope or migrations.
W3C (nav element) and GOV.UK (table scope) are yes/yes; the focus and IBM sources back accessibility only in general.
Shopify Polaris, W3C (consistent identification), NN/g (design systems) and GOV.UK (pre-built components) are yes/yes.
GoodUI headline and above-the-fold tests plus NN/g scrolling data are yes/yes; GoodUI is one organisation, and the OptiMonk headline test is weak.
Only GoodUI (sticky checkout, repeated bottom CTA) is yes/yes; Zalando, Facebook and Netflix back colour or size only.
GoodUI (social counts, logos near the CTA, integration logos) and Optimizely (card logos at checkout) are yes/yes.
Only GoodUI (Netflix three-plan comparison) is yes/yes; the hidden-fee study is yes/weak and the decoy and ordering tests back ordering, not side by side.
Only GoodUI (monthly price framing) is yes/yes; the feature-row test is partly.
Only GoodUI (FAQ near the bottom of a short lead gen form) is yes/yes; footer and purchase-reassurance tests back the idea weakly.
Growth.Design (Zapier, 28%), GoodUI (checkout links removed) and Optimizely (cart promotion removed, +5.5M) are yes/yes.
Entropik (contact details), W3C (footer region) and GOV.UK (copyright notice) are yes/yes.
GOV.UK (one banner, task info in main content), NN/g (banner blindness) and Optimizely (cart banner removed) are yes/yes.
